                                         Introdu tion

  In [M1, M2℄, Milnor de ned invariants of links, known as the Milnor  (mu-bar) invariants.
In fa t, these invariants are not universally de ned, i.e., if the Milnor invariants of order less
than n do not vanish, then those of order n are either not de ned, or at best, they have
indetermina ies. On the other hand, nite-type (or Vassiliev) invariants [Va, Gu, Ko, B2℄
are universally de ned invariants (i.e., for all links). Thus the naively posed question \Are
Milnor's invariants of nite type?" is not well-posed.

   In [HL1℄, the notion of string link was introdu ed, together with the philosophy that
Milnor's invariants are a tually invariants of string links. Indetermina ies are determined
pre isely by the indetermina y of representing a link as the losure of a string link. This
philosophy led to the lassi ation of links up to (link) homotopy.
   From this point of view, the well-posed question \Are Milnor's invariants of string links
of nite type?" was answered aÆrmatively by D. Bar-Natan in [B1℄ and by X. S. Lin in [L℄.
(See also remarks 11.3 and 12.8.)
   Sin e the Milnor invariants are derived from (expansions of) the longitudes of a link, and
sin e the longitudes determine (and are determined by) the Artin representation of a string
link (ea h generator is onjugated by its longitude), one may (in the philosophy of [HL1℄)
de ne the `Universal' Milnor invariant of a string link to be its Artin representation. This
point of view was ontinued in [HL2℄, where the true indetermina y of Milnor's on ordan e
 invariants was determined.
   In the present paper we address the relationship between Milnor's on ordan e invariants
(of string links), i.e., the Artin representation, and the Kontsevi h integral. Sin e nite type
invariants are de ned dually to the Vassiliev ltration, and sin e the Kontsevi h integral is
the universal nite type invariant, they should be al ulable dire tly from the Kontsevi h
integral.
   One of the main results of this paper is that this is possible. Spe i ally, in Theorem 6.1,
we show the following. First, we prove that the ltration on string links indu ed by Milnor's
invariants oin ides with what we all the Z t - ltration, that is, the ltration indu ed by a
  ertain quotient Z t of the Kontsevi h integral, obtained by killing all diagrams ontaining
loops. (The t in Z t stands for tree diagrams, whi h generate the quotient.) And se ond, we
give a ombinatorial formula to ompute the rst non-vanishing Milnor invariants of a string
link  from the rst non-vanishing term of Z t ( ) 1. Although the orresponding result in
the ase of Milnor's homotopy invariants is nearly a tautology, and ertainly suggested by
[B1℄, this formula does not seem to have been dis overed elsewhere.
   The ombinatorial formula given in Theorem 6.1 generalizes to a formula (see Theorem
12.7) whi h expresses the full Magnus expansion of the longitudes in terms of the Kontsevi h
integral. (This formula grew out of a dis ussion with D. Bar-Natan in January 1997.) In
prin iple, this formula allows one to al ulate all the Milnor invariants, not just the rst
non-vanishing ones, although its expli it form for the higher order invariants depends on a
  ertain unipotent automorphism (see remark 12.8).
   The idea that Milnor's invariants are related to tree diagrams had been around before
(the se ond-named author learned about it from D. Bar-Natan and L. Rozansky in summer
1995). From the physi s viewpoint, a onne tion between Milnor invariants and Feynman
diagrams whi h are trees seems to have appeared for the rst time in L. Rozansky's work [R℄.
However, it is remarkable that already before that, one had the `Bing doubling' onstru tion
of T. Co hran [Co2℄, realizing `realizable' Milnor invariants, starting from trees.
   Sin e Milnor's invariants are on ordan e invariants, the above suggests that the redu ed
Kontsevi h integral Z t might be the universal nite type on ordan e invariant. We show
that this is indeed the ase. While for string links this may be dedu ed from the above
relationship between Z t and Milnor's invariants (see remark 14.3), taking this approa h for
general tangles would require a generalization of the stru ture theorem of [HL2℄. There is,
however, a dire t proof whi h we give in Theorems 14.1 and 15.1. This proof relies on the
                    THE KONTSEVICH INTEGRAL AND MILNOR'S INVARIANTS                               3



  ombinatorial omputation of the Kontsevi h integral [Ca, B3, LM1, LM2, KT℄. For this we
were parti ularly in uen ed by T. Le and J. Murakami's point of view.
   A onsequen e of this is that there are no rational nite type on ordan e invariants of
string links other than Milnor's invariants and their produ ts ( orollary 6.4). (We understand
that this result, whi h was originally onje tured by X. S. Lin, has also been obtained
by T. Stanford and D. Thurston [ST℄.) This generalizes a result of K. Y. Ng [Ng℄, who
showed that there are no non-trivial rational nite type on ordan e invariants of knots. In
parti ular, nite type on ordan e invariants miss the `trans nite' on ordan e invariants of
J. Y. Le Dimet [D℄ and T. Co hran and K. Orr [CO℄.
   The Kontsevi h expansion Z takes values in rational ve tor spa es generated by diagrams
and it is an open problem to determine its image on links or string links. This image is a
priori not ontained in the latti e generated by diagrams (sin e Z has rational oeÆ ients).
Our formula allows us to determine expli itly the latti e given by the possible values of
the rst non-vanishing term of the redu ed Kontsevi h integral Z t . See remark 8.2 for the
answer.
   Another appli ation of theorem 6.1 is that the Kontsevi h integral of a link with vanishing
Milnor invariants an be expressed as a sum of treeless diagrams.
   There are several known onstru tions of links with given Milnor invariants [O, HL2, Co1,
Co2℄. One of the byprodu ts of our onsiderations about Milnor invariants is a onstru tion
of string links whose rst non-vanishing term in its Kontsevi h expansion is an arbitrarily
given integer linear ombination of onne ted diagrams. This `realization' result is obtained
using a pro edure, pioneered by T. Stanford [S℄, whi h modi es a link by a pure braid.
In parti ular (at least rationally), this onstru tion also produ es links with given Milnor
invariants.
   In the appendix, as an appli ation of our methods, we give a new and di erent proof of
the fa t, shown re ently by D. Bar-Natan [B4℄, that the Vassiliev ltration of the group ring
of the pure braid group (that is, the ltration indu ed by the Vassiliev ltration on string
links), oin ides with the `horizontal' Vassiliev ltration.

   By a framed tangle, we mean a tangle equipped with a non-vanishing normal ve tor eld,
su h that the restri tion to the boundary is the restri tion of a xed unit ve tor eld normal
to R in C . Isotopy and on ordan e of framed tangles are de ned in the obvious way. Two
framed tangles will be onsidered to be homotopi if their underlying tangles are homotopi .
Note. The terminology `framing' is slightly abusive here, as the non-vanishing normal ve tor

whi h ase a se ond se tion may be determined using the orientation of C  I). Note that for
a knot, an isotopy lass of framing may be spe i ed by an integer, known as the self-linking
number or writhe.
Convention. All tangles, links, and string links, will be onsidered to be framed. A on or-
dan e of tangles will also be assumed to be framed. Pure braids will be equipped with the
zero framing (i.e., the framing indu ing the zero framing on the losure of ea h omponent).
   The set of isotopy lasses of framed tangles form a ategory T , where the obje ts are
  nite sets of points in R (equipped with the standard framing), and omposition is given by
(verti al) sta king. Composition1 will be denoted by (T1 ; T2 ) 7! T1 T2 . (Our onvention is
to put the tangle T2 above the tangle T1 . The domain of the tangle T1 T2 will be denoted
X1 X2 . It is obtained from the disjoint union of X1 and X2 by identifying 1 X1 with 0 X2 .)
The tangle ategory has a monoidal (or tensorial) stru ture2 given by the juxtaposition of
tangles (i.e., one puts one tangle to the right of the other), denoted by (T1 ; T2 ) 7! T1  T2 .
The set of isotopy lasses of l- omponent framed string links will be denoted by SL(l). Note
that string links need not have inverses, so that SL(l) is not a group but only a monoid.
   By Artin's theorem [A℄, two pure braids whi h are isotopi as string links are already
isotopi as braids, i.e., via a horizontal isotopy. Thus isotopy lasses of l- omponent pure
braids form a subgroup P B (l) of SL(l). The inverse of a pure braid  is  = R Æ  Æ r,
where R is the re e tion through a horizontal plane (i.e., R : C  I ! C `I is given by

sends tj to 1 tj ).
   Con ordan e lasses of tangles also form a monoidal ategory CT . The set of framed
  on ordan e lasses of l- omponent framed string links will be denoted by CSL(l). It is
well-known that CSL(l) is a group. The inverse of a string link  up to on ordan e is again
represented by  (see for example [D℄). See gure 10 in se tion 14 for an example.
   Similarly, homotopy lasses of tangles form a monoidal ategory HT . Homotopy lasses
of l- omponent string links form a group HSL(l), with  again inverse to  . It is well-known
that any string link is homotopi to a pure braid (see [HL1℄), and that on ordan e of string

CSL(l). (Not every string link is on ordant to a pure braid.)
   Finally, sin e isotopy of tangles implies on ordan e, and on ordan e implies homotopy,
we have forgetful fun tors, T ! CT and CT ! HT .

The Vassiliev ltration. Let X be a tangle type, that is, a 1-manifold whose boundary

  We de ne the Vassiliev ltration to be the ltration of the linearized ategory Q T by
powers of the augmentation ideal, that is, the ideal generated by di eren es of tangles of the
same type. In other words, one has that Q T (X )1 is generated by di eren es T1 T2 , where
T2 is obtained from T1 by a rossing hange or a hange of framing.3 The n-th term of the
 ltration is generated by ompositions of n elements of ltration 1. Thus, the ltration is
multipli ative with respe t to the juxtaposition and omposition of tangles.
  We denote the n-th term of the Vassiliev ltration on Q T (X ) by Q T (X )n. The indu ed l-
trations on the ve tor spa es Q CT (X ) and Q HT (X ) and on the algebras Q P B (l), Q CSL(l),
and Q HSL(l), will again be alled the Vassiliev ltrations and denoted by Q CT (X )n ,
Q HT (X )n , and so on.

                               3. The universal invariant Z (T ).
    The original Kontsevi h integral [Ko, B2℄ asso iates to every (unframed) knot K in S 3 , an
invariant, whi h is an element of the quotient of A(S 1 ) by the ideal generated by the hord
diagram having a single hord. Although this onstru tion an be extended to tangles, we
  nd it onvenient to use a ombinatorial version of it, based ultimately on seminal work
of Drinfel'd [D1, D2℄. This ombinatorial version has been studied by Le and Murakami
[LM1, LM2℄, Bar-Natan [B3℄, Cartier [Ca℄, Kassel and Turaev [KT℄. This approa h repla es
tangles by q -tangles ( alled non-asso iative tangles in [B3℄).
    The ategory of q -tangles is de ned as follows. A q -stru ture on an ordered set is a bra k-
eting; for example, the bra ketings of the set f1; 2; 3; 4g are (((12)3)4); ((12)(34)); ((1(23))4);
(1(2(34))); (1((23)4)). (See [LM1, LM2, B3, KT℄ for a formal de nition.) A q -tangle is a
tangle equipped with a q -stru ture on i X , for i = 0; 1. Framed q -tangles again are the
morphisms of a monoidal ategory, the obje ts of whi h are obje ts of the framed tangle
 ategory but equipped with a q -stru ture. For example, the identity string link with two
di erent q -stru tures at the top and at the bottom is an isomorphism (and not an identity)
in this ategory. Composition of q -tangles is again given by sta king in the obvious way6 ,
and the monoidal produ t is again given by juxtaposition, where, by way of example, the
bra keting of the juxtaposition of (1(23)) and (45) is ((1(23))(45)). By abuse of notation,
we again denote this ategory by T .
    By the q -type of the q -tangle, we mean the type of the tangle, together with the q -stru ture
on i X , i = 0; 1. Note that the set of q -tangles of a given q -type is naturally in bije tion
with the set of tangles of the underlying type, so that the forgetful fun tor from the q -
tangle ategory to the tangle ategory is a bije tion on morphisms. In parti ular, the set of
endomorphisms of the identity obje t (represented by the empty set of points) of the framed
q -tangle ategory is just the set of isotopy lasses of framed links.
    To a framed q -tangle T : X ! C  I, the ombinatorial version of the Kontsevi h integral
asso iates an element Z (T ),7 whi h lies in (the graded ompletion of) A(X ). It is an isotopy
invariant of the framed q -tangle. (In fa t, one may allow ambient isotopies of C  I whi h
preserve R   I set-wise, whi h is why only the order of the points in i X is important.)

   7

   One has that Z (T ) is multipli ative (i.e., Z (T1 T2 ) = Z (T1 )Z (T2 )) and also monoidal (i.e.,
Z (T1  T2 ) = Z (T1 ) Z (T2 )). This latter property is one advantage of using q -tangles, as it
allows one to ompute the Kontsevi h integral of a link lo ally, by utting it into elementary
morphisms in the q -tangle ategory.
3.1. Remarks. (i) It is sometimes useful to view A as a ategory with the same obje ts
as the tangle ategory T , and with morphisms given by linear ombinations of diagrams on
1-manifolds (i.e., tangle types). Then A is a monoidal ategory (with monoidal stru ture
indu ed by juxtaposition), and Z is a monoidal fun tor from the ategory of q -tangles to A.8
    (ii) The following terminology is sometimes useful. To every obje t of the tangle ategory,
one asso iates an obje t of the q -tangle ategory by giving it the so- alled anoni al q -
stru ture. Here, the anoni al q -stru ture of an ordered set is the one obtained by su essively
taking the bra keting of the prede essors of an element with the element. For example,
(((12)3)4) is the anoni al bra keting of the ordered set f1; 2; 3; 4g.
    (iii) The fun tor Z depends on the hoi e of a ertain element  of A(3) alled the
asso iator. This is the image under Z of the identity 3- omponent string link with the
 anoni al q -stru ture at the bottom and the other q -stru ture at the top. It is hosen so as
to satisfy ertain properties (e.g., to ensure isotopy invarian e). By Drinfeld's work, we an
(and do) hoose an asso iator whose non-zero terms all lie in even degrees.9 This ensures
properties 3.2.6 and 3.2.7 below.
    (iv) Unless stated otherwise, in this paper string links will be equipped with the same
q -stru ture at the top and at the bottom. For a string link  , the rst (i.e., lowest degree)
non-vanishing term of Z ( ) 1 does not depend on the q -stru ture.
Notation. In this paper, the expression O(n) will be used to denote terms of degree greater
than or equal to n.
3.2. Some properties of Z (T ).
    1. One has Z (T ) = 1 + O(1), where we denote by 1 2 A0 (X ) = Q the diagram X [ with
        empty dashed graph . Note that if  is an l- omponent string link, Z ( ) lies in the

              4. The Hopfian monoidal ategory quotients Ah and At .
   We say that A is a monoidal ategory quotient of A, if for all 1-manifolds X , A(X ) is
a graded quotient of A(X ) and the produ t A(X1 ) A(X2 ) ! A(X1 X2 ) and monoidal
produ t A(X1 ) A(X2 ) ! A(X1 q X2 ) pass to maps on quotients. If in addition, the
 omultipli ation A(X ) ! A(X ) A(X ) passes to maps on quotients, the monoidal ategory
quotient is referred to as Hop an. We denote by Z (T ), the image of Z (T ) in A(X ) (where
T : X ! C  I).
   In [B1℄, the Hop an monoidal ategory quotient Ah of A was de ned to be the quotient by
the relations generated by hord diagrams ontaining a hord between the same omponent.
It follows (see [B1℄) that any trivalent diagram ontaining a dashed omponent whi h is
either not simply onne ted, or whi h has two edges on the same solid omponent, is also a
relation. We denote Z by Z h .
   The supers ript h here stands for `homotopy'. Indeed, D. Bar-Natan [B1℄ has shown that
the graded ve tor spa e asso iated to Q HSL(l) with respe t to the Vassiliev ltration is
pre isely Ah (l). Moreover, it is easy to see that Z h is the universal nite type invariant of
tangles up to (link) homotopy. In other words, one has the analogue of the exa t sequen e
of 3.3, with Q T (X ) repla ed by Q HT (X ), and Zn repla ed by Zh n , so that Z h indu es the
Vassiliev ltration on Q HT (X ).
   Similarly, let A = At (and let Z be denoted by Z t ), where all trivalent diagrams ontaining
a non-simply onne ted dashed omponent are onsidered as relations. At is also a Hop an
monoidal ategory

Chinese hara ters.12 There is a natural isomorphism of A(l) with B (l), the Q algebra
of Chinese hara ters, i.e., uni-trivalent vertex-oriented (dashed) graphs, modulo AS and
IHX relations, whose univalent verti es are labelled by elements of the set f1; : : : ; lg. (See
[B2, B1℄.) This restri ts to an isomorphism between P (l) and C (l), the spa e of onne ted
Chinese hara ters. The multipli ation in the algebra B (l) is given by disjoint union, so that
B (l) is the ommutative polynomial algebra on C (l). The isomorphism of A(l) with B (l) is
 omultipli ative but not multipli ative.13
   The isomorphism between A(l) and B (l) passes to an isomorphism between Ah (l) and
B (l), where B h (l) is the ommutative polynomial algebra on the spa e C h (l) of labelled
  h
Chinese hara ters whi h are trees with distin t labels. The proof given in [B1℄ also shows
that it passes to an isomorphism between At (l) and B t (l), where B t (l) is the ommutative
polynomial algebra on the spa e C t (l) of labelled Chinese hara ters whi h are trees.

The Artin representation and the longitudes. Let F (l) be the free group on x1 ; : : : ; xl .

                                An : SL(l) ! Aut0(F (l)=F (l)n+1)
de ned as follows. Let  be a string link with l omponents. Consider the in lusions i0
and i1 of the omplement of the l standard points p1 ; : : : ; pl , in C  0 and in C  1 (see

fundamental groups. Identifying the fundamental group of the omplement of p1 ; : : : ; pl in

that
                                      An()(xi) = ixii 1;
where i = (in) 2 F (l)=F (l)n+1 is the longitude of  de ned as follows. The framing

                     10. The ase of homotopy Milnor invariants.

   We re all the onstru tion of the homotopy Milnor invariants. The redu ed free group

 ommutes with all of its onjugates. Consider a string link  2 SL(l) and its i-th longitude

under the quotient map whi h sets the i-th generator xi equal to 1. Then Ri ( ) depends
only on the homotopy lass of  , i.e., the value of  in HSL(l).
   We say that  has homotopy Milnor ltration n, if all longitudes Ri ( ) are trivial in
RF (l 1)=RF (l 1)n .

de omposition P B (k) = F (k 1) o P B (k 1)).

free (see [HL1℄).
   Next, re all that for a group G, the augmentation ideal I  Q G is generated by the set
of elements g 1 where g 2 G. The ltration of Q G by powers of I is alled the I -adi
  ltration. It is a general fa t (see e.g. [Q1, or. 4.2℄) that if Gm =Gm+1 is torsion free for
all m, then for all n, Gn is equal to fg 2 G : g 1 2 I ng, the so- alled n-th dimension
subgroup. Applying this to G = HSL(l) shows that (ii) and (iii) are equivalent.
   The equivalen e of (iii) and (iv) follows from the following proposition and the fa t (see
se tion 4) that Z h indu es the Vassiliev ltration on Q HSL(l).

Remark 11.3. There are several proofs [B1, L℄ that Milnor's invariants are of nite type.
Here, we brie y sket h how to see this using the above methods. It suÆ es to show that the
map whi h takes a string link to its longitude is a ltration preserving map, i.e., it sends
the Vassiliev ltration to the I -adi ltration of the group ring (of the nilpotent ompletion)
of the free group (sin e the Magnus expansion is multipli ative and hen e preserves I -adi
  ltrations).

a map of group algebras whi h preserves the I -adi ltrations. Sin e taking the (homotopy)
longitudes is by de nition su h a proje tion, the result follows in the homotopy ase.
22                          NATHAN HABEGGER AND GREGOR MASBAUM



   In the general ase, note that it suÆ es to ompose with the Magnus expansion, sin e
this is a ltration preserving isomorphism. Applying the operation D, whi h doubles ea h
 omponent N times say, and then redu ing to homotopy, we see that this gives inje tions of
the asso iated power series rings, up to order N 1. Consequently, the general ase follows
from the result for homotopy.

                    12. A global formula for Milnor's invariants.
   The ombinatorial formula given in Theorem 6.1, whi h des ribes the rst non-vanishing
Milnor invariants, is quite suggestive, sin e it is obtained from the doubling operation via
a forgetful map. One an think of the map ji (i.e., take the sum over all i-labelled verti es

              16. Appendix on the Vassiliev filtration of pure braids.
   We de ne the Vassiliev ltration on Q P B (l) to be the ltration indu ed by the Vassiliev
  ltration on string links, i.e., we put Q P B (l)n = Q P B (l) \ Q SL(l)n . Let I denote the aug-
mentation ideal of Q P B (l). Let A0 (l) be the graded ompleted subalgebra of A(l) generated
by hord diagrams in degree 1 between distin t omponents. A0 (l) is a Hopf subalgebra.
Theorem 16.1. (i) The Vassiliev ltration on Q P B (l) oin ides with the I -adi ltration,
i.e., one has I n = Q P B (l) \ Q SL(l)n .
   (ii) Moreover, Z indu es an isomorphism (of omplete Hopf algebras) from the I -adi
 ompletion of Q P B (l), to A0 (l).
Note. Sin e A0 (l) inje ts into At (l), one may repla e Z by Z t in 16.1(ii).
Remark 16.2. It is easy to see that the I -adi ltration on pure braids orresponds to
the ltration `a la Vassiliev' where one allows only `horizontal' rossings, i.e., oming from
`singular' braids (all strands remaining verti al).21 It has been known for some time (see
[K1, K2℄), that this ltration orresponds to the Hopf algebra a la Vassiliev of `horizontal'
 hord diagrams and `horizontal' 4T relations. Theorem 16.1 says that this algebra inje ts
into the Hopf algebra At (l), and a fortiori into A(l). (This latter has re ently been proven
in a di erent way by Bar-Natan [B4℄.)

Corollary 16.5. The redu ed Kontsevi h integral Z t (and a fortiori the Kontsevi h integral
Z ) separates pure braids.
Proof. In view of lemma 16.4, it suÆ es to show that the interse tion of the lower entral
series of P B (l) is trivial. This is well-known [FR℄, but for ompleteness, here is a proof.
The pure braid group is a semidire t produ t P B (l) = F (l 1) o P B (l 1). Moreover, the
a tion of P B (l 1) on the free group F (l 1) is via the Artin representation. Then, sin e
this representation a ts trivially on homology, it is an exer ise to see that the lower entral
series of P B (l) is the semidire t produ t of the lower entral series of F (l 1) and that of
P B (l 1). Sin e the interse tion of the lower entral series of a free group is trivial, by
indu tion, the same holds for the pure braid group.
Remark 16.6. Sin e the lower entral series quotients of the free group are torsion free,
the argument above also shows that the lower entral series quotients P B (l)n=P B (l)n+1 are
torsion free, and hen e the pure braid group P B (l) is residually torsion free nilpotent. By
Chen [C, 2.2.1℄, this implies that the I -adi ltration of the group ring Q P B (l) is omplete,
i.e., satis es \I n = 0. By 16.1, the same is true for the Vassiliev ltration on pure braids.
